processing_steps.method: conventional melting-casting route in an open-air induction furnace (Power Trak 250-10 R Inductotherm)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cast ingot of the designed Fe-8Mn-5Al-0.2C steel; cast specimen shows dual-phase δ-ferrite + austenite.
Cast ingot homogenized at 1100 °C for 2 hr before hot forging.

processing_steps.method: hot forging followed by air cooling to room temperature
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Hot forged to 50% thickness reduction in the temperature range 1050–800 °C following air cooling to room temperature.
Hot forged samples further hot rolled after soaking at 1100 °C for 2 hr.

processing_steps.method: hot rolling in two passes with intermediate reheating at 1100 °C for 5 min, followed by water quenching from the finish rolling temperature
processing_steps.cooling_medium: water quenching from finish rolling temperature (~800 °C)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Hot rolled in the range 1050–800 °C in two passes (reheating at 1100 °C for 5 min between passes), 50% reduction per pass, finally water quenched to room temperature; gives the hot rolled & quenched (HRQ) 3 mm sheet that is the parent of the IA750_5 Min sample.

processing_steps.method: surface machining up to 1 mm depth on both sides of the hot rolled sheet to remove the oxide layer
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Gives 3 mm thick hot rolled sheet used for intercritical annealing.

processing_steps.method: intercritical annealing at 750 °C (IA750) for 5 minutes, followed by air cooling to room temperature
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The 5 min condition defines the IA750_5 Min sample; 750 °C was chosen from the δ+γ duplex region of the Thermo-Calc equilibrium phase-fraction plot.

structures.overall_structure: After intercritical annealing at 750 °C for 5 min the previously formed martensite (from the HRQ condition) starts dissolving/transforming into intercritical ferrite (α) and needle-shaped reverted austenite; δ-ferrite morphology stays unchanged (highly stable) and untransformed austenite remains.
structures.number_of_phases: 4 (δ-ferrite, untransformed austenite, reverted austenite, intercritical ferrite α)

phases_present.morphology: island-like/elongated, structure and morphology remain unchanged after intercritical annealing (highly stable δ-ferrite)

phases_present.volume_fraction: ~27% (formation of ~27% reverted austenite through dissolution of martensite at 5 min annealing)
phases_present.morphology: needle shape (sharp needles), red arrow in Fig. 4A2
phases_present.grain_size: needle length (major axis) 2.829±0.30 µm and width (minor axis) 0.350±0.20 µm

average_grain_size.value: length (major axis) 2.829±0.30 µm; width (minor axis) 0.350±0.20 µm

microstructure_list.region: adjacent to reverted austenite (former martensite matrix)

phases_present.morphology: fine ferritic constituent formed by dissolution of martensite (yellow plus sign in Fig. 4A2 marks an α-ferrite spot)

defects.dislocation_density: dislocation density reduced by annealing for 5 minutes (no quantitative value reported)

phases_present.volume_fraction: ~46% total austenite (untransformed + reverted) before tensile test; ~42% after tensile test
phases_present.morphology: blocky/elongated untransformed austenite (white arrow in Fig. 4A1)

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Annealing for 5 minutes reduces the dislocation density in the microstructure, resulting in slightly lower stress; no quantitative dislocation density given.

interfaces.phase_evolution: At 5 min, martensite (from HRQ) begins dissolving/transforming into intercritical ferrite (α) and needle-shaped reverted austenite; δ-ferrite is highly stable and unchanged. With longer annealing reverted austenite progressively dissolves into intercritical ferrite via elemental partitioning.
interfaces.interface_notes: The interface between intercritical ferrite and reverted austenite is characterised at nanoscale in the paper (HRTEM/APT) for the IA750_60 Min specimen, showing Mn and C enrichment with Al and Fe depletion at the boundary; for the IA750_5 Min specimen only SEM-EDS phase compositions are reported.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: subsize specimen per ASTM E8/E8M, machined by wire EDM along the rolling direction
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: at least three samples tested and average reported; engineering stress-strain curves in Fig. 6A1

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curves of HRQ and 750 °C/5-180 min specimens shown in Fig. 6A1; true stress-strain curves in Fig. 6A2 (IA750_5 Min curve shown in green).
strain_hardening_rate: mean work-hardening rate in stage S2 between 1100–400 MPa

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: nanoindentation with diamond Berkovich tip (B-T 50, tip radius 100 nm, tip angle 142.3°)
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: indentation load 30 mN; linear loading and unloading rate 60 mN/min; dwell time 10 s; Anton Paar NHT1000038550

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Product of ultimate tensile strength and total elongation (PSE) / TRIP effect; IA750_5 Min PSE = 2.5 GPa% vs the optimum IA750_60 Min PSE = 7.9 GPa%

characterization_methods.technique: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with Energy Dispersive X-ray analysis (EDAX)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS VP 300 FEG-SEM equipped with EDAX; at least 5-7 areas and 15-20 spots averaged per phase
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 2 µm scale-bar high-magnification images and EDS spot analyses of δ-ferrite, untransformed austenite and needle-shaped reverted austenite
characterization_methods.purpose: Resolve phase morphology and quantify elemental composition of individual phases in the IA750_5 Min specimen
characterization_methods.key_findings: δ-ferrite Al 5.37±0.05, Mn 7.09±0.09 wt.%; untransformed austenite Al 4.50±0.14, Mn 8.07±0.11 wt.%; reverted austenite Al 4.43±0.05, Mn 8.30±0.20 wt.%; not much variation of Al and Mn between δ-ferrite and untransformed austenite compared to the rolled & quenched specimen.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Bruker D8 advanced X-ray diffractometer, Co-Kα (1.79 Å), step size 0.02°, 2θ range 20°–120°
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: before and after tensile testing (Fig. 7a, b)
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify phases and quantify austenite volume fraction (retained/reverted) before and after deformation
characterization_methods.key_findings: IA750_5 Min austenite volume fraction ~46% before and ~42% after tensile test (transformation ratio ~8.7%).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Anton Paar NHT1000038550 with diamond Berkovich tip (B-T 50; tip radius 100 nm, tip angle 142.3°)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: indentation load 30 mN; loading/unloading rate 60 mN/min; dwell 10 s; load-displacement curves in Fig. 5 (B1-B3)
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure nano-hardness of δ-ferrite, untransformed austenite and reverted austenite regions of the IA750_5 Min specimen
characterization_methods.key_findings: δ-ferrite 4267±264 MPa; untransformed austenite 4351±575 MPa; reverted austenite 3867±110 MPa.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; strain rate 2.67×10^-4 s^-1; subsize specimens per ASTM E8/E8M machined by wire EDM along RD
characterization_methods.purpose: Evaluate mechanical properties (YS, UTS, TE) of the IA750_5 Min specimen
characterization_methods.key_findings: YS 460±8 MPa, UTS 605±7 MPa, TE 4.15±0.80%, PSE 2.5 GPa%.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 10 µm scale-bar fractograph of the IA750_5 Min specimen
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterise the fracture mode of the tensile-tested IA750_5 Min specimen
characterization_methods.key_findings: δ-ferrite shows cleavage mode of fracture while the retained austenite (untransformed + reverted austenite) shows quasi-cleavage mode of fracture.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Fe-8Mn-5Al-0.2C designed composition, equilibrium phase fractions vs temperature (Fig. 1b)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Predicted δ+γ duplex region (~650 °C to ~1350 °C) used to select the 750 °C intercritical annealing temperature; compared with dilatometry of the hot-forged sample (Fig. 1c) which showed only an insignificant contraction.

analytical_models.model_name: Equilibrium phase fraction / critical temperature calculation
analytical_models.equation_role: Predict critical temperatures and phase fractions to justify IA temperature
analytical_models.model_note: Used to set the intercritical annealing temperature of 750 °C shared by the IA750 series including the IA750_5 Min sample.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Austenite composition, grain size (assumed 40 µm), temperature; assumes finer austenite grain of 40 µm
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Theoretical SFE of the designed steel ~35 mJ/m²; for the IA750_60 Min reverted austenite SFE recalculated to ~27 mJ/m² using measured Mn (7.58±0.14) and Al (3.96±0.15) contents.

analytical_models.equation_role: Compute SFE of austenite from Gibbs free energy change and interfacial energy
analytical_models.model_note: Assumed austenite grain size of 40 µm. The high SFE implies TWIP as the major deformation mechanism by design, but actual deformation was TRIP due to changed composition/morphology of reverted austenite.

unmapped_findings: For the IA750_5 Min specimen, the product of ultimate tensile strength and total elongation (PSE) is 2.5 GPa% (Table 3); PSE is defined as the product of UTS and total elongation.

Austenite volume fraction of the IA750_5 Min specimen: ~46% before tensile test and ~42% after tensile test, giving a transformation ratio of ~8.7% (K, mechanical stability of austenite ≈ 1.93), indicating relatively higher mechanical stability than the HRQ specimen.
The ~46% austenite fraction after 5 min annealing confirms formation of ~27% reverted austenite through dissolution of martensite.

The IA750_5 Min specimen shows higher mechanical stability of austenite (reverted austenite enriched in Mn, similar to untransformed austenite, and lean in C) and consequently a low TRIP effect, giving lower UTS and TE than the optimum IA750_60 Min condition.
Density of the developed alloy measured by Archimedes' principle is 6.91455 g/cc, ~11.35% lower than conventional steel (~7.8 g/cc) — reported for the alloy (all IA750 series share the same alloy).

The theoretical SFE of the designed steel is ~35 mJ/m² (within the 20-40 mJ/m² TWIP range), whereas the reverted austenite is Mn-lean (smaller needle size) at longer annealing times and its SFE changes with composition/morphology.
